name: Form & Space
description: An architecture portfolio with conceptual case studies and reference photography.

slides.title: Space shaped by daily life
items: My work begins with how a place is used across an ordinary day. Arrival, changing light and the movement between shared and private areas become the basis for the plan.

The following fictional projects explore a courtyard home, a neighbourhood library and a compact workspace. Stock reference photographs illustrate the intended atmosphere. They are visual references for the concepts presented here.

slides.title: Three studies in inhabitation
items: A compact home organised around a protected outdoor room. The study tests how a shared centre can bring daylight into the plan while preserving quieter edges for reading and rest.

A public interior arranged around different levels of activity. A clear arrival space connects the collection, shared tables and a quieter reading area, allowing visitors to choose where they feel comfortable.

slides.title: Courtyard House
items: How can a small home feel open without exposing every room to the street? The concept places the main outdoor space inside the plan and uses the perimeter to moderate views.

Shared rooms address the courtyard while service spaces occupy the outer edge. Openings are considered in relation to neighbouring properties, and the entrance creates a gradual transition from public approach to private life.

slides.title: A sequence of thresholds
items: The entrance is designed as a short sequence rather than a single exposed opening. A covered pause gives residents time to arrive before the view opens toward the shared interior.
Rooms meet through deliberate changes in width and light. The concept uses these transitions to distinguish social areas from quieter spaces while maintaining a legible route through the house.

slides.title: Neighbourhood Library
items: A small public library must support conversation and concentration within the same interior. The study asks how the plan can make these different activities understandable without relying on constant signage.

The welcome desk faces the entrance and the busiest tables sit nearby. Shelving provides a gradual transition toward quieter seats. Clear sightlines help staff remain available while allowing visitors to settle independently.

slides.title: Light as a working material
items: The design studies where useful daylight reaches the room and where direct glare could interrupt reading or work. Openings are evaluated against furniture placement instead of being treated as an isolated facade pattern.

Artificial lighting supports the same hierarchy after sunset. General illumination defines the route, while local light serves reading and working positions. The intention is a comfortable transition between different times of day.

slides.title: A room for focused work
items: The workspace concept supports a small team with both shared tasks and periods of concentration. Its limited footprint requires each zone to have a clear purpose and an accessible relationship to the others.

A central worktable anchors the shared area. Storage forms a useful boundary beside the quieter seats, and a small meeting zone remains close to the entrance so visitors can arrive without crossing every workspace.

slides.title: Material choices with a purpose
items: Materials are selected in relation to the surfaces people use most. Handles, seats and worktops need different qualities from walls viewed at a distance. The study considers maintenance alongside colour and texture.

The proposal favours details that can be explained clearly in a drawing and reviewed with the fabricator. Junctions between materials receive attention early, when changes can still improve both appearance and construction.

slides.title: A process that makes decisions visible
items: I use diagrams and simple models to compare the consequences of different plans. Each study addresses a specific question, such as the length of an arrival route or the depth of a shared room.

The selected approach is translated into coordinated drawings and a material study. Reviews focus on unresolved relationships between use, structure and enclosure before the design moves into more detailed work.

slides.title: From concept to conversation
items: I am interested in small buildings and interiors where careful planning can change everyday experience. A useful brief describes who will use the space, what currently causes difficulty and what the project must achieve.
An initial discussion reviews the site information, ambitions and constraints. The next stage is a defined study that identifies the design questions and the material needed to answer them.
